description: Rive Gauche is a Saint Laurent line name, used across several shapes rather than one single silhouette. Most often it points to the soft, unlined shopping tote in canvas or leather carrying the house's Rive Gauche lettering, a nod to Yves Saint Laurent's original Rive Gauche ready-to-wear line. Because the name covers more than one bag, check the exact shape and material against the listing before assuming a model.
note: Line/collection name, not a single model.

description: The Low Key is a Louis Vuitton hobo, a soft slouchy shoulder bag introduced in recent seasons in Monogram canvas and grained leather. It reads more relaxed than the house's structured icons, with a curved top and a single shoulder strap. We can describe the shape confidently; we're leaving the debut year off until we can source it precisely.
note: Contemporary model; debut year not yet sourced.

description: Shopping Tote is a Saint Laurent category name rather than one named model. It covers the house's large open totes, most recognizably the East/West shopper in smooth or grained leather with the cassandre logo. Sizes and leathers vary, so match the exact version to the listing before pinning down details.
note: Category/descriptor, not a single model.

description: The Tote Bag is Marc Jacobs' canvas shopper printed with the oversized MARC JACOBS logo, sold in several sizes from mini to large. It became a genuine viral hit on social media for its price point and bold lettering, and has stayed a steady seller since. The exact launch year is widely reported as around 2020 but we haven't pinned an official date, so we're leaving it off.
note: Viral hit; precise debut year not officially sourced.

description: The City Steamer is a structured top-handle bag Nicolas Ghesquiere designed for Louis Vuitton, drawing on the house's early Steamer travel bag. It has a firm trapezoidal body, twin rolled handles, and the LV initials on the front hardware, and comes in several sizes. It arrived as a new pillar of Ghesquiere's handbag lineup in the mid-2010s.
note: Ghesquiere-era design; exact debut year not crisply sourced.

description: Dome is a shape descriptor for a rounded, domed-top handbag rather than one specific Gucci model. Gucci has used dome silhouettes across lines, so the name here likely points to a bag by its shape. Check the hardware, leather, and any line branding against the listing to identify the exact style.
note: Shape descriptor, not a single named model.

description: The Lockit is one of Louis Vuitton's older handbag names, a rounded tote with a padlock closure inspired by the house's travel trunks. It first launched in 1958 and has been reissued over the decades in Monogram canvas and leather. If you're dating a specific one, the hardware and leather tell you which era it's from.

The Liz is an MCM tote, a structured shopper carried in the brand's Visetos logo-coated canvas with leather trim. It sits in MCM's everyday tote range, roomy and open-topped with twin handles. We can describe the shape and material; we don't have a sourced debut year, so it's left off.
note: Debut year not sourced.

description: Bucket refers to Louis Vuitton's bucket-shaped shoulder bags rather than one single model. The most famous is the Petit and Grand Noe, possibly the original drawstring bucket from 1932, alongside later versions like the NeoNoe. Because several LV buckets exist, confirm which one the listing means before assuming a year or size.
note: Category/shape name covering several LV bucket models.

description: On My Side is a Louis Vuitton tote built on a mix of Monogram and smooth calf leather, a large everyday shoulder bag with a clean modern face rather than an all-over logo. It sits in the house's contemporary tote range. We're leaving the debut year off until it's sourced.
note: Contemporary model; debut year not sourced.

description: The Falabella is Stella McCartney's signature bag and the house's best known, a vegan tote trimmed in the diamond-cut whipstitched chain. Stella McCartney's own account dates its debut to the Winter 2009 collection, with the body chain moving to lighter aluminum in 2010 (some retailers cite 2010 as the debut). It's been a cornerstone of the brand's animal-free luxury story ever since.
note: House says Winter 2009; some retailers say 2010.

description: La Medusa is Versace's structured top-handle bag, named for the house's Medusa head emblem that sits as a gold plaque on the front. Versace introduced it in its Spring/Summer 2021 campaign as the season's new handbag design, and it comes in several sizes from mini to a larger top-handle. The hardware and the Greek-key detailing are the tells.

The Woody is Chloe's canvas tote, easy to spot by the woven logo ribbon patch and cotton webbing strap, sold in canvas with leather trim across a few sizes. It became a street-style and social-media favorite in the early 2020s. Worth knowing: buyers have flagged that the logo patch on some pieces is heat-pressed rather than embroidered, so check yours against the version you expect.
note: Rose to fame early 2020s; exact debut year not crisply sourced.

description: The Danube is a Louis Vuitton crossbody, a small round-cornered messenger with a long adjustable strap and a flap or zip top, historically in Monogram canvas and reissued in later seasons. It's one of the house's compact everyday styles. We don't have a sourced debut year, so it's left off.
note: Real LV model; debut year not sourced.

description: Uniform is not one of Chanel's retail handbag models. Chanel Uniform is the line of pieces made for the house's own boutique and staff uniforms, which occasionally surface on the secondhand market. If a bag is labeled this way, treat the name as a sourcing note about its origin, not an official model name, and verify what the actual silhouette is.
note: NOT a retail model; Chanel staff/boutique uniform program. Removal/merge candidate.

description: The Cabata is Christian Louboutin's tote, most recognizable in its spiked-stud version where metal spikes stud the leather, though it also comes in a plainer soft calf. It's a two-handle open tote, often reversible on the studded model. We can describe the design confidently; we're leaving the debut year off until it's sourced.
note: Debut year not sourced.

description: The Avenue Sling is a Louis Vuitton men's crossbody sling bag, a compact body-worn pack usually in Damier or Monogram canvas with an adjustable strap meant to be worn across the chest or back. It sits in LV's men's bag range. Debut year isn't sourced here, so it's left off.
note: Debut year not sourced.

description: Le 37 is a Saint Laurent bucket bag, a soft drawstring shoulder bag tied to the house's Rive Gauche heritage. It has a slouchy round body and the cassandre logo. We're leaving the debut year off until we can source it.
note: Contemporary model; debut year not sourced.

description: Easy Pouch On Strap describes a Louis Vuitton format rather than one legacy model, a flat zip pouch that comes with a wide detachable shoulder strap and often a removable inner clutch. It's sold in Monogram Empreinte leather and canvas. Because it's a format used across seasons, match the exact material and size to the listing.
note: Format/descriptor name, not a single legacy model.

description: The Hug is a Salvatore Ferragamo shoulder bag whose soft, gathered body is designed to look like it hugs the wearer's side, closed with the house's signature Gancini hook hardware. It's a contemporary design in smooth leather. We don't have a sourced debut year, so it's left off.
note: Debut year not sourced.

description: The Wallace is a Bottega Veneta hobo, a soft slouchy shoulder bag in the house's woven intrecciato leather with a rounded body and a single strap. It predates the Daniel Lee headline bags and is less commonly seen today. We haven't sourced a firm debut year, so it's left off.
note: Older intrecciato hobo; debut year not sourced.

description: The Marais is a Louis Vuitton name used over the years for more than one shape, from the older Bucket-style Marais in Epi leather to later totes. Because the name spans eras and silhouettes, identify the exact version by its leather and shape before dating it. We're leaving the year off for that reason.
note: Real LV name reused across shapes/eras.

description: The Trouville is a Louis Vuitton handbag, a compact structured top-handle in Monogram canvas with a zip top and short handles, a popular 1990s and 2000s style now firmly in the vintage market (it also appeared in the Murakami Multicolore run). If you're dating one, the canvas and hardware place its era. We haven't sourced an exact debut year, so it's left off.
note: Real vintage LV model; exact debut year not sourced.

description: The Hampstead is a Louis Vuitton tote, a structured shopper historically made in Damier Ebene canvas with twin handles and a zip or snap top, aimed at everyday carry. It's now largely a vintage-market style. We don't have a sourced debut year, so it's left off.
note: Real (largely discontinued) LV model; debut year not sourced.

description: The Trio Messenger is a Louis Vuitton men's messenger built from three attachable pouches that clip together, usually in Monogram or Taiga leather, worn crossbody. The modular three-pouch construction is its signature. Debut year isn't sourced here, so it's left off.
note: Contemporary men's model; debut year not sourced.

description: The S Lock is a Louis Vuitton line built around an S-shaped clasp, appearing across styles including a sling and a messenger, largely in the men's range. Because the name covers more than one shape, the S-clasp is the constant to look for. We're leaving the debut year off until it's sourced.
note: Line built on the S-clasp, spans several shapes.

description: The Babylone is a Louis Vuitton tote named after the Rue de Babylone neighborhood in Paris. The original was a shoulder tote from the late 1980s made into the early 2000s, and the name was later revived for the Babylone in Monogram Empreinte leather. If you're dating one, the leather and construction separate the vintage from the modern.
note: Original late-1980s tote, later revived in Empreinte; exact debut year not pinned.

description: The Pochette Marly is a Louis Vuitton flap pouch, a small structured shoulder bag with a front flap, historically in Monogram canvas, now mostly a vintage-market piece. It sits among LV's compact 1990s and 2000s styles. We haven't sourced an exact debut year, so it's left off.
note: Real vintage LV model; debut year not sourced.

description: The Locky BB is a Louis Vuitton top-handle in Monogram canvas with a leather flap and a distinctive front lock, worn by the handle or on a shoulder strap. The BB marks it as the small size in LV's naming. Debut year isn't sourced here, so it's left off.
note: Real LV model; debut year not sourced.

description: The Dior Vibe is Dior's sporty line, introduced from the Cruise 2022 show and unveiled in early 2022, drawing on athletic and Y2K bowling-bag shapes with a sneaker-inspired base and CD hardware. It comes as a hobo, bowling bag, and top-handle. The soft rounded silhouette and rubberized detailing are the tells.
note: Line name spanning several shapes; debut year 2022 sourced.
